svg.title: Multimodal annotation pipeline
svg.desc: Dataset readers retain native fields, units, calibration and clocks, and keep every readable part of an episode when another part is damaged. An optional text LLM interprets field meanings. Dataset publisher declarations are retained. Optional field definitions supplied by the dataset publisher or user can override model-inferred meanings and layouts. Code checks recording quality. Annotation settings specify the capture setup, model, frame sampling, evidence inspection and field dictionary. Long episodes are split into API requests with episode-relative timestamps and marked API boundaries. A text LLM reads teleop task descriptions to select the needed image detail; UMI and human ego use fixed starting resolutions. Code prepares visual frames, recorded robot state, actions, tactile arrays, depth and other signals and assembles data-dependent prompts and output schemas. For a recording with depth, a touch sensor or fields the prompt does not carry (any recording with --inspection all), the annotation model chooses fields and windows, code reads samples or images, and results return to it for at most two rounds. The final VLM annotates behavior, object state changes, scene relationships, data issues, operator mistakes, recoveries and sensor findings; for tactile arrays, a separate VLM pass compares regional responses. Code parses responses, checks evidence citations and stitches request parts onto the episode timeline. The annotation model, in one text-only call, chooses the few sensor findings shown as cards on the video. The board build scores each episode and subgoal, and the JSON export includes usable annotations, every sensor finding, the scores and reported gaps. The recovery example illustrates model findings; separate recording-quality checks are exported alongside annotations. Recorded RGB, tactile, depth and state examples illustrate saved model annotations. A paired handoff example shows an operator mistake and its recovery.
